stem: An unsensitized Rh(D)-negative pregnant client receives Rho(D) immune globulin at 28 weeks. Which explanation best describes the purpose of this therapy?

options.A: It removes maternal anti-D antibodies that have already caused fetal hemolysis.
options.B: It changes fetal Rh antigen expression for the remainder of pregnancy.
options.C: It helps prevent maternal Rh immunization after exposure to Rh-positive fetal red blood cells.
options.D: The 28-week dose generally replaces postpartum prophylaxis if the pregnancy remains uncomplicated and maternal antibody screening stays negative.

rationale: RhoGAM contains IgG anti-D and is indicated to prevent Rh immunization in Rh-negative patients exposed to Rh-positive red blood cells; the prescribing information states that it suppresses the immune response to Rh-positive red cells, although the precise mechanism is unknown. It does not reverse Rh immunization once it has occurred and does not change fetal Rh antigen expression. Routine antepartum prophylaxis at 26–28 weeks also does not generally replace postpartum prophylaxis: if the newborn is Rh-positive, the label states that a postpartum dose is essential when antepartum prophylaxis was indicated, subject to the label's specific dosing exceptions.
educational_objective: Explain that antepartum Rho(D) immune globulin is prophylaxis against maternal Rh immunization after exposure to Rh-positive fetal red blood cells, not treatment of established sensitization.

source_claim_supported: RhoGAM is indicated to prevent Rh immunization in Rh-negative women in pregnancy-related exposures; §2.1 lists prophylaxis at 26–28 weeks and states postpartum dosing is essential if the infant is Rh-positive when antepartum prophylaxis is indicated; §12.1 states RhoGAM suppresses the immune response to Rh-positive red cells and is not effective once Rh immunization has occurred.

source_original.stem: An unsensitized Rh(D)-negative pregnant client receives Rho(D) immune globulin at 28 weeks. Which explanation best describes the purpose of this therapy?

options.A: It removes maternal anti-D antibodies that have already caused fetal hemolysis.
options.B: It changes fetal Rh antigen expression for the remainder of pregnancy.
options.C: It helps prevent maternal Rh immunization after exposure to Rh-positive fetal red cells.
options.D: The 28-week dose generally replaces postpartum prophylaxis if the pregnancy remains uncomplicated and maternal antibody screening stays negative.

source_original.rationale: Rho(D) immune globulin provides passive anti-D that suppresses maternal immunization after exposure to Rh-positive fetal red cells. It prevents sensitization; it does not treat established fetal hemolytic disease or change fetal Rh type. Antepartum prophylaxis does not automatically eliminate postpartum dosing when the newborn is Rh-positive.
source_original.source_detail: DailyMed RhoGAM Ultra-Filtered PLUS label — Indications/Usage and obstetric dosing: prevention of Rh immunization, routine antepartum prophylaxis at 26–28 weeks and postpartum prophylaxis when indicated. Current FDA RhoGAM label at the exact DailyMed set ID; live version rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies; medication administration, adverse effects/interactions and monitoring. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the stem, answer set, and key because the construct is current and unambiguous. Rewrote the rationale to preserve the label's exact level of certainty: RhoGAM contains IgG anti-D and suppresses Rh immunization, but the mechanism is unknown. Clarified that postpartum prophylaxis remains indicated for an Rh-positive newborn subject to specific label exceptions, rather than making an absolute dosing statement.

audit_findings.source_authority: Exact current DailyMed biologic prescribing information for RhoGAM Ultra-Filtered PLUS.
audit_findings.currentness: Current label is Version 19; revised July 2025 and rechecked 2026-08-16.
audit_findings.exact_locator: §1.1 supports prevention indication; §2.1 supports 26–28 week antepartum and postpartum dosing relationship; §12.1 supports immune-response suppression and ineffectiveness after sensitization.
audit_findings.claim_audit: The final rationale does not overstate the mechanism and preserves specific dosing qualifications.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because RhoGAM is prophylactic and does not reverse established Rh immunization or fetal hemolysis.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect; the product does not alter fetal Rh antigen expression.
distractor_audit.C: Directly supported prevention purpose and uniquely best.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because the label explicitly maintains postpartum prophylaxis when the infant is Rh-positive after indicated antepartum prophylaxis, apart from defined exceptions.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C correctly states the therapeutic purpose; D conflicts with the labeled postpartum requirement.
audit_findings.cueing: Distractors are clinically related to Rh disease/prophylaxis and the key is not identifiable from wording alone.
audit_findings.blueprint: NCSBN 2026 Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies includes medication administration, medication education, and response evaluation.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Adversarial review checked the postpartum-dose exception and mechanism-of-action wording; final text avoids turning either into an unsupported universal rule.
